/u/catechumen mentioned a police department "putting a more positive spin" on a wiki page. I'm not sure about the LAPD case but the NYPD also came under fire supposedly for doing the same things in relation to the Eric Garner case. Here is the list of all changes they made:

  • "Garner raised both his arms in the air" changed to "Garner flailed his arms about as he spoke."

  • chokehold changed to chokehold or headlock in one instance

  • push[ed] Garner's face into the sidewalk changed to push[ed] Garner's head down into the sidewalk

  • paramedics who responded to Garner after he was put in a chokehold changed to paramedics who responded to Garner's respiratory distress

All but the second are substantially more accurate. He was absolutely flailing his arms. Paramedics aren't called when a chokehold is used, they're called when there is a medical emergency. And as anybody can clearly see in the video the officers don't push his face into the sidewalk, they make a concerted effort to push him down on the side of his head. The second change is dodgy. It may have been the officer's intent to perform a headlock but it was certainly a chokehold as was verified by the autopsy. In any case it's certainly no grand conspiracy. Just somebody who probably didn't think what was written was accurate and decided to do their best to improve the article. But of course the "pushing his face into the sidewalk" line is now still in the article, in the second paragraph no less. That's wikipedia for you.
